get_object.description: Read one object's full record by its system number: its titles, descriptions, makers and their roles, dates, places, materials, techniques, categories, styles, measurements, marks and inscriptions, gallery label, where it is now and its images.

mock_response.brief_description: Teapot, silver with wooden details, Birmingham hallmarks for 1922-23, mark of Napper and Davenport, designed by Robert Johnson.
gallery_labels:
CUBE TEAPOT
Silver, the finial and handle of wood
Hallmarks for Birmingham 1922-23
marks_and_inscriptions:
Base: stamped: “The Cube Tea Pot
Robert Johnsons Patents
Gt Britain 110951
USA 1380066-21
Napper and Davenport
Birmingham England
Serial No. L31
mock_response.materials_and_techniques: Silver, with hinged lid and black wooden handle and finial.
mock_response.object_history: Its production in silver by the Birmingham retail silversmith, Napper & Davenport gave it an aesthetic importance that the original patentee never initially intended.
mock_response.summary_description: Stylistically, this teapot appears to be an English interpretation of the aesthetic principles of the German Bauhaus. However, the patent details inscribed on the base reveal that the design was registered in 1916, three years before the Bauhaus existed.
mock_response.title: Teapot

description: Explore the Victoria and Albert Museum's collection of art, design and performance: search over a million objects by maker, material, place, style, category, date and more, read an object's full record, get its images at any size, count a search's objects per maker or material, and search the V&A archives. A trigger starts a workflow when the V&A adds or changes a matching object. No account or API key required.
